questions.q: A price rise of {p}% leads to a fall in quantity demanded of {q}%. Calculate the PED.
questions.why: −{q} ÷ {p} = {answer}. Size below 1 is inelastic, above 1 elastic.

questions.q: The price falls from £{p1} to £{p2} and quantity demanded rises from {q1} to {q2}. Calculate the PED.
Incomes rise by {y}% and demand for a good changes by {q}%. Calculate the YED.
questions.why: {q} ÷ {y} = {answer}. A negative value means an inferior good.

questions.q: The price of good B rises by {p}%, and demand for good A changes by {q}%. Calculate the XED of A with respect to B's price.
questions.why: {q} ÷ {p} = {answer}. Positive means substitutes, negative means complements.

questions.q: A firm sells 1,000 units at £{p}. PED is {e}. If it raises its price by 10%, what is its new total revenue?
questions.why: Quantity changes by {e} × 10%. New price × new quantity = {answer}.

questions.q: Demand for a good is price inelastic. What happens to total revenue if the firm raises its price?
questions.why: Quantity falls by a smaller percentage than the price rises, so revenue rises.

questions.q: Which is likely to make demand for a product more price elastic?
options: It takes up a tiny share of income
questions.why: With close substitutes available, buyers switch easily when the price rises.

questions.q: Why is demand for petrol usually more elastic in the long run than the short run?
options: People have time to find alternatives, such as a more efficient car
questions.why: Over time, people can change how they travel and what they drive.

questions.q: Match each result to its meaning.
questions.why: For YED and XED, the sign carries the meaning.

questions.q: A YED of 0.3 means the good is an inferior good.
questions.why: A positive YED means a normal good. A value below 1 means it is income inelastic, often a necessity.

questions.q: Explain why a government might choose to tax a good with price inelastic demand.

ideas.label: Quantity demanded falls by only a small amount when the price rises
So the tax raises a lot of revenue

questions.model: If demand is price inelastic, quantity demanded falls by a smaller percentage than price rises, so people still buy. The tax is paid on most of the original sales, so it raises a lot of revenue for the government.
questions.why: Inelastic demand means the tax base barely shrinks.

tests.answer: People still buy it when the price rises so the government gets lots of tax revenue.
It raises revenue for the government.
Because the government likes taxing things.
